messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bulgarian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bulgarian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Тази смирена Италия ще бъде спасението за което умря девицата Камила, Евриал и Туно и Нисо са ранени.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Di | Preposition introducing the genitive “of that” | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | quella | Demonstrative “that” specifying Italy | Тази | “this/that” | OK | | umile | Attribute “humble” describing Italy | смирена | “humble” | OK | | Italia | Proper noun “Italy” | Италия | “Italy” | OK | | fia | Future copular verb “shall be” | ще бъде | “will be” | OK | | salute | Noun “salvation” (subject complement) | спасението | “the salvation” | OK | | per | Preposition introducing causal clause “for which” | за | “for” | OK | | cui | Relative pronoun referring to the salvation | което | “which” | OK | | morì | Simple past “died” | умря | “died” | OK | | la | Definite article (feminine singular) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | vergine | Noun “virgin” (title/epithet) | девицата | “the virgin” | OK | | Cammilla | Proper name “Camilla” | Камила | “Camilla” | OK | | Eurialo | Proper name “Euryalus” | Евриал | “Euryalus” | OK | | e | Coordinating conjunction “and” (first) | и | “and” | OK | | Turno | Proper name “Turnus” | Туно | “Turnus” | OK | | e | Coordinating conjunction “and” (second) | и | “and” | OK | | Niso | Proper name “Nisus” | Нисо | “Nisus” | OK | | di | Preposition “of” introducing the participial phrase | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | ferute | Past participle used adjectivally “wounded” | ранени | “wounded” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *Di*, *la*, *di* – Bulgarian does not need a separate preposition or article in these positions; their semantic contribution is absorbed elsewhere in the sentence. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bulgarian script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bulgarian text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
